correctness.rationale: For arbitrary fixed Hadamard ratio q>1 and exceptional indices Λ={N_j}, the compressed multiplier matrix B_ji=a_{N_j+ℓ−N_i} has constant diagonal a_ℓ. The off-diagonal multiplicity for a fixed positive difference N_j−N_i is bounded by the number of N_j in [t,q t/(q−1)], which is uniformly finite; the lower triangular part is eventually zero. Because bounded φ has ℓ² Taylor coefficients, B−a_ℓI is Hilbert–Schmidt. A tail invertibility bound transfers square-summability of the complementary Fourier coefficients of φ^n into square-summability of the lacunary coefficients, using φ^{n+1}=φφ^n and geometric decay of finitely many low coefficients. The reverse weighted-to-unweighted inclusion thus holds for all q>1. The other direction follows from monotone H² powers and the lacunary charging inequality N_j u_{N_j}≤q/(q−1)Σ_{n=N_{j−1}+1}^{N_j}u_n. Necessity follows by Paley H¹ lacunary projection and a bounded outer-function modulus concentrated on separated arcs E_k to force divergence when inf N_jβ_{N_j}=0. Source finite checker is corroboration, not all-q proof.
